Use the universal property of the quotient by the ring congruence \(c\).

First establish the defining factorization:
\[
\operatorname{RingCon.lift}(f,H)\circ \operatorname{RingCon.mk'}=f.
\]
This is the second conjunct and should follow directly from the computation rule for `RingCon.lift`.

For uniqueness, use that `RingCon.mk'` is surjective. To show
\[
g=\operatorname{RingCon.lift}(f,H),
\]
apply extensionality (or quotient induction) and compare both maps on representatives `RingCon.mk' x`. The hypothesis `Hg` evaluates \(g(\mathrm{mk'}\,x)\) to \(f(x)\), while the lift computation rule gives the same value for `RingCon.lift`.

The essential role of \(H:c\leq\ker f\) is to ensure that \(f\) is constant on \(c\)-equivalence classes, so the induced homomorphism on the quotient is well-defined.
